title: Studio Campaign Ops
intro: Studio markets gear across email, social and web, and every campaign is the same machine wearing different copy: a brief becomes one message, the message becomes three channel renditions, the renditions clear an approval chain, and Friday's rollup says what worked. One mistake here is public - the wrong price emailed to forty thousand people. You are going to build the content operation: one source of truth, many renditions, tracking codes from a policy, an approval chain that resets when anyone edits, and a rollup that joins on the codes. Then it meets a week where someone edits mid-chain, someone types a code by hand, and someone changes a price.

world.oneLiner: Studio Outdoor launches campaigns across email, social and web from one approved message, tracks each channel by code, and rolls up performance every Friday.

roles.name: Campaign Manager
roles.does: Writes the brief: product, price, offer, headline, launch date.

roles.name: Copywriter
roles.does: Drafts and edits the message, and is the first approval in the chain.

roles.name: Channel Specialist
roles.does: Owns each channel's rendition and send, and hears when a rendition or a code is wrong.

roles.name: Marketing DL
roles.does: The distribution list that receives the Friday rollup.

world.deliverable: a launch package per campaign with every channel approved, and the Friday rollup
world.clock: A brief lands and its renditions exist within the hour; reviews arrive in order through the week; the launch package goes out when the chain is complete. Friday 4:00 PM: the rollup joins every channel's numbers by tracking code.
world.stakes: Get it wrong and a channel sends a price the message never had, an edited message goes out on an old approval, or Friday's rollup silently drops the channel whose code did not match.

builds.title: One source of truth

builds.goal: Every channel will say the same thing because every channel is built from one record: product, price, offer, headline. Create it from the brief, version 1, status draft.
builds.outcome: Every brief becomes one row in Content Records at version 1.
constraints: One record per campaign - add or replace by campaignId.
version starts at 1; status starts as draft.

builds.title: Three renditions, one message
builds.brief: Render the message for each channel from its rules, with a tracking code from the policy.
builds.goal: Each channel wraps the message differently and has its own length limit; those rules live in a table. The tracking code is built from a policy, not typed. Loop over the rules and write one rendition per channel: text, whether it fits, and its code.
builds.outcome: Every campaign has one row per channel in Renditions, with text from the rules, a code from the policy, and fits.
constraints: Loop over Rendition Rules; do not write three steps.
text = prefix + headline + '. ' + product + ', now ' + price + '. ' + offer + suffix.
code = policy prefix + '-' + campaignId + '-' + channel.
fits = len(text) <= maxLength.

hints.nudge: Lookup Tracking Code Policy ('1.0.0', policy); Lookup Rendition Rules, all rows (rules); For each over rules: Transform text = concat(prefix, parent.headline, '. ', parent.product, ', now ', parent.price, '. ', parent.offer, suffix), code = concat(parent.policy.prefix, '-', parent.campaignId, '-', channel), fits = len(text) <= maxLength, campaignId = parent.campaignId, version = 1; Store into Renditions, add or replace by campaignId, channel.
steps: Before the Store, add a Lookup on Tracking Code Policy where version = '1.0.0' (policy) and a Lookup on Rendition Rules, all rows (rules).
Add a For each over rules.

Inside: Transform campaignId = parent.campaignId, version = 1, text = concat(prefix, parent.headline, '. ', parent.product, ', now ', parent.price, '. ', parent.offer, suffix), code = concat(parent.policy.prefix, '-', parent.campaignId, '-', channel), fits = len(text) <= maxLength.
Inside: Store into Renditions, add or replace if it exists, same row when campaignId, channel. Run it.

builds.brief: A Channel Specialist may tune a channel's wording. Apply the edit to that rendition.

builds.outcome: A rendition edit updates that channel's text and nothing else.
constraints: Update the existing rendition; the row is the same when campaignId and channel match.

builds.title: The approval chain
builds.brief: Three approvals launch the campaign; a rejection sends it back with a new version.
builds.goal: Copywriter, Brand Reviewer, Marketing Director. Each approval is captured with the version it approved. When three approvals are in, the campaign launches: every rendition goes into the Launch Package with its send time, and the Channel Specialist is told. A rejection or an edit bumps the version, and the Copywriter is told.
builds.outcome: Approvals are captured; three of them launch the package for every channel; a rejection or edit increments the version and logs rework.
constraints: Capture every approval in Approvals with its version.
Launch = the package for every channel, with sendAt from the Send Schedule, and launchedOn = the review that completed the chain.
Not approved: version + 1 on the record, a rework row, the Copywriter told.

hints.question: Who has to say yes before 40,000 people get the email, and in what order?
hints.nudge: Lookup Content Records (record); Condition decision == approved: YES lane Store into Approvals; Lookup Approvals all where campaignId = campaignId (done); Transform count = len(done); Condition count == 3 -> launch (update record status, Lookup Renditions all, For each: Lookup Send Schedule, Transform (sendAt, launchedOn, version = parent.record.version), Store into Launch Package, Send). NO lane: Transform version = record.version + 1; Store update Content Records; Store into Rework; Send to Copywriter.
steps: Open the Reviews flow, connect it to Reviews, and Lookup Content Records where campaignId = campaignId (record).

Condition: decision == approved. NO lane: Transform version = record.version + 1; Store into Content Records, update by campaignId; Store into Rework; Send to Copywriter ('{{campaignId}} back to you: {{decision}} by {{reviewer}}').
YES lane: Store into Approvals. Then Lookup Approvals, all rows where campaignId = campaignId (done). Transform count = len(done).

YES lane, then: Condition count == 3. Its YES lane: Transform status = 'approved'; Store into Content Records, update by campaignId; Lookup Renditions all where campaignId = campaignId (rends); For each over rends: Lookup Send Schedule where channel = channel (sched); Transform sendAt = sched.sendAt, launchedOn = parent.reviewId, version = parent.record.version; Store into Launch Package, add or replace by campaignId, channel; Send to Channel Specialist ('Launch {{campaignId}} {{channel}} at {{sendAt}}').
Run it.

builds.title: The Friday rollup
builds.brief: Join every channel's numbers to its campaign by tracking code, and send the rollup.
builds.goal: Clicks and opens land in the Performance Events table tagged with a code. The code is the join: look each event's code up in Renditions to know which campaign and channel it belongs to. Total the week, send the rollup to Marketing, archive it.
builds.outcome: Every performance event is joined to its campaign and channel in Rollup Rows; the rollup carries totalClicks; a copy is archived.
constraints: Join by code - look the code up in Renditions.
totalClicks = the sum of clicks over the events.

hints.question: How does Friday know that 640 clicks belong to the social post and not the email?
hints.nudge: Lookup Performance Events all (events); For each: Lookup Renditions where code = code (rendition); Transform campaignId = rendition.campaignId; Store into Rollup Rows. After the loop: Transform totalClicks = sum(events, 'clicks'); Compose; Send to Marketing DL; Store into Campaign Archive.
steps: Open the Friday rollup flow. Lookup Performance Events, all rows (events). For each over events.
Inside: Lookup Renditions where code = code (rendition); Transform campaignId = rendition.campaignId; Store into Rollup Rows.
After the loop: Transform totalClicks = sum(events, 'clicks'). Compose rollup with {{totalClicks}} and {{#each events}}- {{channel}} {{code}} {{clicks}}{{/each}}.
Send to Marketing DL with {{rollup}}; Store into Campaign Archive.

builds.title: Week 2: an edit mid-chain
builds.brief: An approval of version 1 does not carry to version 2. Count approvals for the current version only.
builds.goal: The Copywriter approved the Ridge Pack message, then edited the headline. Brand and the Director approved the edited version. Run your Week 1 flow: three approvals are on record, and the campaign launches - with one approval for text nobody else saw. Any edit resets the chain: only approvals of the current version count.
builds.outcome: The campaign launches only when three approvals exist for the record's current version; the edit bumped the version and everyone earlier in the chain re-approves.
constraints: count = the approvals whose version equals the record's current version.
An edit is rework: version + 1, logged, Copywriter told.
The launch records which review completed the chain.

builds.title: Week 2: the code typed by hand
builds.brief: An event whose code matches nothing must be flagged, not dropped.
builds.goal: Social's numbers came in under 'ridge_social_promo' - a code somebody typed instead of taking it from the policy. Run your Week 1 rollup: the join finds nothing, and the 400 clicks vanish from the campaign. When a code matches no rendition, log the event as unmatched, count it in the rollup, and tell the Channel Specialist.
builds.outcome: Unmatched events are logged and counted in the rollup, the Channel Specialist is told, and matched events still join.
constraints: An unmatched event is a row in Unmatched Events, not a silent skip.
The rollup carries unmatched = how many.

builds.title: Week 3: the wrong price
builds.brief: A hand edit that changes the price is rejected before it can send.
builds.goal: The Summit Jacket campaign is approved. Then a Channel Specialist tightens the email copy and types 199 where the record says 249. Run your flow: the edit is applied, and the launch package now emails a price the message never had. A rendition must still carry the record's price; an edit that does not is rejected, and the Campaign Manager is told.
builds.outcome: A rendition edit whose text does not contain the record's price is rejected and logged; the rendition is unchanged; the Campaign Manager is told.
constraints: Compare the edit's text with the price on the Content Record.
A rejected edit changes nothing.
Tell the Campaign Manager, who owns the price.
